## What you'll practice

- Choosing a dataset, selecting two variables, and classifying them by type.
- Producing univariate descriptive statistics in Stata.
- Building a do-file that reproduces your descriptive output.

## Introduction

This is the first of four PS2 workshop sessions (Weeks 8–11). Each workshop gives you one hour of structured work time to make progress on your Problem Set 2 submission, with support from your seminar leader.

Today's goal is to choose a dataset, select two variables, and produce univariate descriptive statistics in Stata. By the end of this session you should have a working do-file that reproduces your descriptive output.

You will need the [PS2 instructions](https://emckclac-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/k2588471_kcl_ac_uk/IQBi2GOzRRuhRZ_CuKGFQkxxAb9qYjIkeDR-dwKAfe-2Muo?e=dQPCaW), the [model answer](https://emckclac-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/k2588471_kcl_ac_uk/IQAFECuB8PAkTY1SYwdKD5lYAU_4xlmM9elWyHYXMieTFu4?e=Da3UAy), and the [Shared Project Folder](https://emckclac-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/k2588471_kcl_ac_uk/IgC7Jh31fuDKQZCWFPMDyHegAXyh48OD-lIbeoHj73LmQHs?e=H4mk5p) (which contains the datasets, codebooks, and do-files).

## Task 1: Read the PS2 instructions and model answer

Open the PS2 instructions and read through the five required sections of the report. Then open the model answer to see what a completed submission looks like.

Pay attention to the decision rule table in the instructions — it tells you which statistical test and chart your variable combination will require.

## Task 2: Choose a dataset and explore variables

Choose one of the four datasets from the `data-raw` folder:

- British Election Study (BES)
- Quality of Government (QoG)
- Brexit Regional dataset
- National Student Survey (NSS)

Open the dataset in Stata and browse it alongside the relevant codebook. Identify variables that could form an interesting pair for a correlational research question. For each variable, classify it as **nominal** or **numeric**.

## Task 3: Produce univariate descriptive statistics

Produce appropriate univariate descriptive statistics for each of your variables:

- **Nominal variables:** frequency table (`tabulate`) or bar chart.
- **Numeric variables:** summary statistics (`summarize`) and/or histogram.

Check for missing values. If there are observations with missing data on either variable, decide whether to drop them before proceeding. This matters because the number of observations should be consistent across your descriptive and bivariate output.

## Task 4: Start building your do-file

Create a new do-file and add the commands you have run so far. Your do-file should:

- Set the working directory and load the dataset.
- Produce the univariate descriptive output for both variables.
- Include comments explaining what each section of code does.

Test the do-file by running it from top to bottom. It should execute without errors and reproduce all the output you have generated.

## By the end of today you should have

- A dataset and two variables selected, with both classified by type.
- Univariate descriptive output for both variables produced in Stata.
- A do-file that runs from top to bottom and reproduces the univariate output.

If you have reached these milestones, you are on track. Next week's workshop will focus on producing the bivariate visualisation and running the hypothesis test.
